CODELEARN · F8 — MY PROGRESS DASHBOARD

FER202 final assignment (mini LMS) · Function 8 of 11 · Starter = reference of F7 · Suggested time: 75 minutes · Total: 10 marks

1. Overview

One page that answers "how am I doing?". Everything is derived from data you already load: the student's enrolments (+ lesson totals, F6) and their quiz attempts (results). No new collection, no counters stored anywhere — numbers are recomputed from the server data every time the page opens, so they can never drift.

API calls

RequestUsed for
GET /enrollments?userId=…&_expand=course… + GET /lessons?courseId=…per-course progress (F5/F6 thunk)
GET /results?userId=…&_expand=chapter&_sort=submittedAt&_order=descquiz history with chapter titles, newest first

The five numbers

IdMeaning
#stat-enrolledcourses enrolled
#stat-completedcourses at 100% (and having at least one lesson)
#stat-lessonscompleted lessons across all courses
#stat-quizzesdistinct chapters with at least one passed attempt (passing the same quiz twice counts once)
#stat-avgaverage percent of all attempts, rounded, e.g. "67%"; no attempts ⇒ "—"

Edge cases

  • No enrolments ⇒ #no-progress; no attempts ⇒ #no-quiz-history and average "—".
  • A result whose chapter was deleted still shows (fallback text), the page must not crash.

Main features

  • Summary numbers · Per-course table · Quiz history · Empty states & access

General requirements

  • Continue from your own F7 code (or the starter, which is the F7 reference). Files marked NEW/EDIT in the tree are the ones this step touches.
  • Create React App (React 18), React Router v6, Redux Toolkit, Axios, React-Bootstrap; json-server 0.17.4 on port 9999 (1.x dropped _expand/_embed).
  • Every HTTP call goes through src/api/*.js (one axiosClient with baseURL: process.env.REACT_APP_API_URL); each API function returns response.data itself — do not rely on interceptors (the auto-grader’s axios does not run them).
  • Keep the ids/classes printed in the brief — the auto-grader uses them. Components never call axios directly.

4. Data model

FieldTypeNotes

5. Functional requirements

1. Summary numbers 3 marks

Requirements:

  • Protected route /progress (navbar #nav-progress for students): #stat-enrolled, #stat-completed, #stat-lessons, #stat-quizzes, #stat-avg computed as in the table above.

Must use: reduce Set

Example:

an@codelearn.vn ⇒ 2 · 0 · 3 · 1 · 67%

2. Per-course table 3 marks

Requirements:

  • #progress-table, one tr.progress-row per enrolment (newest first): .progress-course, .progress-lessons "done/total", .progress-percent (ProgressBar "P%"), .progress-best best attempt % for that course or "—".

3. Quiz history 2.5 marks

Requirements:

  • #quiz-history, one tr.quiz-row per attempt, newest first: .quiz-chapter (chapter title via _expand=chapter), .quiz-date dd/mm/yyyy, .quiz-score "S/T (P%)", .quiz-status badge "Passed"/"Failed". Thunk fetchMyResults in the quiz slice.

Must use: _expand=chapter Badge

4. Empty states & access 1.5 marks

Requirements:

  • #no-progress / #no-quiz-history; guests ⇒ /login; loading ⇒ spinner, error ⇒ #progress-error.

6. Element ids / classes used by the auto-grader

SelectorPurpose
#nav-progress · #progress-titlenavigation
#stat-enrolled #stat-completed #stat-lessons #stat-quizzes #stat-avgthe value element itself (text = the number)
#progress-table tr.progress-row .progress-course .progress-lessons .progress-percent .progress-bestcourses table
#quiz-history tr.quiz-row .quiz-chapter .quiz-date .quiz-score .quiz-statushistory table
#no-progress #no-quiz-history #progress-errorstates

7. Grading rubric

#FeatureMarks
1Summary numbers3
2Per-course table3
3Quiz history2.5
4Empty states & access1.5
Total10

Common deductions

  • Counting quiz attempts instead of distinct passed chapters.
  • Storing totals in db.json / localStorage that go stale.
  • Hard-coded http://localhost:9999 in components instead of the .env variable.
  • Mutating Redux/React state, or writing localStorage inside a reducer.
  • App crashes (white screen) on an empty list, an unknown id or a server error.

8. Submission

Work in the editor (files on the right) or download the starter, then npm install and npm run dev (json-server :9999 + React :3000) and paste your files back. Press Run for the sample checks and Submit for full grading (hidden checks included). The reference solution of this step unlocks after an Accepted submission.

CODELEARN · F8 — BẢNG TIẾN ĐỘ CỦA TÔI

Assignment cuối kỳ FER202 (mini LMS) · Chức năng 8/11 · Starter = lời giải F7 · Thời gian gợi ý: 75 phút · Tổng: 10 điểm

1. Tổng quan

Một trang trả lời câu "mình học tới đâu rồi?". Mọi thứ đều suy ra từ dữ liệu đã tải: lượt ghi danh của học viên (+ tổng số bài, F6) và các lượt làm quiz (results). Không thêm bảng mới, không lưu bộ đếm ở đâu cả — mỗi lần mở trang tính lại từ dữ liệu máy chủ nên không bao giờ lệch.

Lời gọi API

RequestDùng cho
GET /enrollments?userId=…&_expand=course… + GET /lessons?courseId=…tiến độ từng khoá (thunk F5/F6)
GET /results?userId=…&_expand=chapter&_sort=submittedAt&_order=desclịch sử quiz kèm tên chương, mới nhất trước

Năm con số

IdÝ nghĩa
#stat-enrolledsố khoá đã ghi danh
#stat-completedsố khoá đạt 100% (và có ít nhất một bài)
#stat-lessonstổng số bài đã hoàn thành
#stat-quizzessố chương khác nhau có ít nhất một lượt đạt (đạt cùng quiz hai lần tính một)
#stat-avgtrung bình percent mọi lượt, làm tròn, vd "67%"; chưa làm lượt nào ⇒ "—"

Trường hợp biên

  • Chưa ghi danh ⇒ #no-progress; chưa làm quiz ⇒ #no-quiz-history và trung bình "—".
  • Kết quả của chương đã bị xoá vẫn hiện (chữ thay thế), trang không được sập.

Chức năng chính

  • Các con số tổng · Bảng từng khoá · Lịch sử quiz · Trạng thái rỗng & quyền

Yêu cầu chung

  • Làm tiếp trên code F7 của chính bạn (hoặc starter = lời giải F7). Tệp đánh dấu NEW/EDIT trong cây là tệp bước này đụng tới.
  • Create React App (React 18), React Router v6, Redux Toolkit, Axios, React-Bootstrap; json-server 0.17.4 cổng 9999 (bản 1.x bỏ _expand/_embed).
  • Mọi lời gọi HTTP đi qua src/api/*.js (một axiosClient với baseURL: process.env.REACT_APP_API_URL); mỗi hàm API tự trả response.data — đừng dựa vào interceptor (axios của máy chấm không chạy interceptor).
  • Giữ đúng id/class in trong đề — máy chấm dùng chúng. Component không gọi axios trực tiếp.

lessons.title: What is React?
lessons.content:
React is a JavaScript library for building user interfaces from small, reusable components.
In this lesson you see how a React app is just a tree of components that turn data into UI.

lessons.title: Create React App & project structure
lessons.content:
Create the project with npx create-react-app, then walk through public/index.html, src/index.js and src/App.js.
Run it with npm start on http://localhost:3000.

lessons.title: JSX and components
lessons.content:
JSX looks like HTML but compiles to React.createElement calls.
A component is a function that returns JSX; its name must start with a capital letter.

lessons.title: Props vs State
lessons.content:
Props are read-only data passed from a parent; state is data a component owns and changes with its setter.
Changing state re-renders the component.

lessons.title: useState and useEffect
lessons.content:
useState stores a value between renders; useEffect runs side effects such as fetching data after the component renders.
Always list the values the effect uses in its dependency array.

lessons.title: let, const and var
lessons.content: Prefer const, use let when a variable must be reassigned, and avoid var (function scope, hoisting surprises).

lessons.title: Primitive types
lessons.content: string, number, boolean, null, undefined, bigint and symbol — and why typeof null is "object".

lessons.title: Arrow functions and array methods
lessons.content: Write short callbacks with arrow functions and transform data with map, filter and reduce without mutating the original array.

lessons.title: Your first Express server
lessons.content: Install express, create an app and call app.listen(3000). Add a GET route that returns JSON.

lessons.title: Routing & middleware
lessons.content: Split routes with express.Router and write middleware with (req, res, next) for logging and validation.

lessons.title: Building a REST API
lessons.content: Map CRUD to HTTP: GET /items, POST /items, PUT /items/:id, DELETE /items/:id — with the right status codes.

lessons.title: SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY
lessons.content: Choose columns with SELECT, filter rows with WHERE and sort the result with ORDER BY.

lessons.title: JOIN in practice
lessons.content: Combine rows of related tables with INNER JOIN and LEFT JOIN on their keys.

questions.content: What does JSX compile to?
questions.explanation: The build tool turns every JSX tag into a React.createElement (or jsx()) call that returns a plain object describing the UI.

questions.content: Which command creates a new React app with Create React App?
questions.explanation: npx downloads and runs create-react-app once, without installing it globally.

questions.content: Which file renders <App /> into #root in a CRA project?
questions.explanation: src/index.js calls ReactDOM.createRoot(document.getElementById("root")).render(<App />).

questions.content: Props are…
options: mutable data owned by the child
read-only data passed from parent to child
questions.explanation: A component must never change its props; the parent owns that data.

questions.content: Why must you never mutate state directly (state.items.push(x))?
options: React compares references, so the same array means no re-render
questions.explanation: Create a new array/object (spread, map, filter) so React sees a new reference and re-renders.

questions.content: Where should state shared by two sibling components live?
options: In their closest common parent (lift state up)
questions.explanation: Lifting state up gives one source of truth; the siblings receive it via props.

questions.content: When does useEffect(fn, []) run?
questions.explanation: An empty dependency array means "after mount" (twice in development StrictMode).

questions.content: What is wrong with calling a hook inside an if statement?
options: Hooks must be called in the same order on every render
Hooks only work in class components
questions.explanation: React matches hook state by call order, so hooks must sit at the top level of the component.

questions.content: Which keyword declares a variable that cannot be reassigned?
questions.explanation: const prevents reassignment (the object it points to can still change).

questions.content: What is typeof null in JavaScript?
questions.explanation: A historic bug kept for compatibility: typeof null === "object".

questions.content: Which value is NOT falsy?
questions.explanation: Any non-empty string, including "0", is truthy.

questions.content: Which method starts an Express server on a port?
questions.explanation: app.listen(port, callback) opens the HTTP server.

questions.content: What does an Express middleware function receive?
questions.explanation: Middleware gets the request, the response and next() to pass control on.
